messages.author: ee7a1845b55c5f1d
messages.subject: Model diagnostics for binomial GLMM
parts:
Hi all,

sorry, this is a pretty basic questions, but I'm wondering what people would suggest as model diagnostics for a binomial GLMM fitted in INLA. 

I'm particularly interested in how well the model fits the data, and not so much in comparing it to alternative models (which I understand I could do with cpo, dic etc.). 
I'm struggling a little bit with the fact that the model is a logistic regression which makes it somewhat difficult to understand in how far the methods for, say, Gaussian models are appropriate.

The model has the following structure:

fit <- inla(formula = binary_response ~ pred1 + pred2 + f(rand1, model = "iid"),
                 data = dat, family =  "binomial",
                 control.family = list(control.link=list(model = "logit"),
                  control.inla = list(correct = TRUE),
                  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo=TRUE, waic = TRUE, po=TRUE,      config=TRUE))

Any suggestions on how to do model diagnostics in INLA would be very much appreciated.

Thanks in advance,
Martin
